question: According to the Enneking (MSTS) staging system, which combination CORRECTLY characterises a Stage IIB bone sarcoma?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes Enneking Stage IA: low-grade (G1), intracompartmental (T1), no metastases (M0). Stage II denotes high-grade tumours.
This is Enneking Stage IIA: high-grade (G2), intracompartmental (T1), no metastases (M0). Stage IIB requires extracompartmental extension.

Correct. Enneking Stage IIB = high-grade (G2) + extracompartmental (T2) + no distant metastases (M0). This is the most common stage at which osteosarcoma and Ewing's sarcoma present, and it mandates neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by wide resection.
The presence of distant metastases defines Enneking Stage III regardless of grade or compartment status. Stage III carries the worst prognosis.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Enneking grid: Grade (G1 low/G2 high) × Compartment (T1 intra/T2 extra) × Metastases (M0/M1). Stage IIB = G2 + T2 + M0.
Excellent. Stage IIB = high-grade + extracompartmental + no metastases — the stage that most commonly requires neoadjuvant chemotherapy + wide resection for limb salvage.
